extracted.intended_audience: improvisational performers, ComedySportz organizers, and general audience/fans
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and operational standards for staging and judging ComedySportz improvisational matches, including match format, referee duties, fouls/penalties, content expectations, audience judging, and organizational/licensing notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traditional match format
rubrics_metrics.description: The traditional format of a ComedySportz match features two teams of improvisational performers ("Players"), competing in various rounds, using improv games and performing scenes. Audience members judge the results and award points as directed by the Referee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matches consist of rounds and improv games/scenes; the competitive team-vs-team structure and games-driven rounds are central to the format. The flavor is similar to Whose Line Is It Anyway? but is a more competitive and For Everyone (content-wise) version of Theatresports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referee role and authority
rubrics_metrics.description: In every match, a ComedySportz referee monitors the action, awarding points, and administering Fouls as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The referee directs scoring and enforces penalties to keep the match moving; referee decisions (including awarding points and calling fouls) are central to match governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Out of Bounds Foul (content restriction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Called when a player uses explicit language or refers to something crass or off-color.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalty: the offending player or audience member must spend the remainder of the game outside the theater space (they may or may not be welcomed back). Historical note: originally called the 'Brown Bag Foul' (player had a brown paper bag placed on their head) but replaced by the 'Out of Bounds Foul' due to COVID-19 in 2022. This enforces the organization's emphasis on clean, family-friendly content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Groaner Foul (pun penalty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any player who speaks a pun bad enough to make the audience groan causing their team to lose one point (or awarding the other team with a point), unless their apology to the audience is heartfelt enough and accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided: 'Why does the Norwegian navy put barcodes on ships? So they can Scandenavian' — such puns can trigger the Groaner Foul. This encourages performers to avoid groan-inducing wordplay or to use timely, acceptable apologies to mitigate penalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spontaneously generated fouls (referee discretion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any spontaneously generated Foul the referee feels is needed to move the match forward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees may invent or call additional fouls as necessary to manage pace, audience engagement, or to correct match flow — emphasizing flexible enforcement and on-the-fly show control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience judging determines outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Match outcomes are not pre-determined as audience voting/selected judges decide the winner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the image of competition is maintained, the final winner is determined by audience votes or selected judges, reinforcing live interaction and audience-focused evaluation rather than scripted outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clean, audience-focused content standard ("For Everyone")
rubrics_metrics.description: The CSz format is a more competitive and For Everyone (content-wise) version of Theatresports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ComedySportz emphasizes clean, family-friendly material so groups can perform for corporate, college, church, school, and association clients and run youth leagues. Performers should avoid explicit or off-color material to meet the organization's client and community expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dynamic team rosters and performer availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Teams are often dynamic, with rosters depending on which player (many of whom have other occupations) are available for a match at any given time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Producers and showrunners should plan for flexible casting and variable team composition; matches retain competitive framing despite roster changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing and organizational structure
rubrics_metrics.description: CSz Worldwide and ComedySportz are licensed by the World Comedy League Incorporated, and there are licensed ComedySportz organizations in multiple cities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To operate under the ComedySportz name and format, local groups are typically licensed; many operate arenas, provide workshops and corporate team-building, and may run high-school/middle-school leagues—implying standards for branding, content, and programming to meet organizational expectations.
